newsitem.title: UK: Allianz ART company will seek US expertise - board.
newsitem.headline: Allianz ART company will seek US expertise - board.

text.p: The Zurich-based alternative risk transfer company being set up by Allianz in the autumn will recruit expertise from the U.S., board member Detlev Bremkamp said in London on Thursday.
"Most of the experience in this field is in the U.S, so that is where we will start looking. But we are also talking to some other high-calibre players in the market," he told Reuters.

Speaking before a rare board meeting in London, Bremkamp accepted the new 500 million Swiss francs unit was being driven more by what competitors were doing than by customer demand from the bottom up, but said it should not be seen as a defensive manoeuvre.
"This is something new for us, it is a testing phase. We have to investigate it because our rivals are because and there may be a market for it," he said.
"Winterthur recently tried something on a small scale and that seemed to work. We will be going the same sort of way," he said.

Bremkamp said the company, which was announced last month and does not yet have a name, will employ around 40 people looking at ways of providing financial insurance and reinsurance against the risk of company balance sheets being affected by interest and currency fluctuations and internal earnings trends.
Bremkamp said the new company would not deal with captive insurance business, which would remain the responsibility of regional subsidiaries.
"We will be using financial instruments such as derivatives," he said. "We will also start offering cat bonds into the market."

He confirmed that the company would also offer traditional reinsurance products. He said some could come from internal business switched away from other reinsurers, but added that to gain the tax benefits of setting up in Switzerland it would have to accept business from other companies as well.
The move is part of Allianz's drive to become the world market leader for industrial insurance, and the unit will have offices in the U.S. and Amsterdam.
